label: Treats rereading as effective review
description: The learner believes going over the material again strengthens memory, when it mainly builds familiarity.

remediation.explanation: Rereading adds exposure; recall adds strength. Turn every reread into a closed-book attempt.

label: Believes highlighting locks material in
description: The learner treats marking sentences as studying them, though highlighting only trains recognition.

remediation.explanation: Highlighting locates text; it does not encode it. It pays off only when the marked material is recalled later.

label: Believes last-minute massing is the efficient strategy
description: The learner concentrates study into one session and expects durable memory from it.

remediation.explanation: Cramming can pass tomorrow's test; spaced study keeps the material a month later. Same hours, better curve.

label: Equates recognising answers with producing them
description: The learner counts 'that looks right' as knowing, then cannot produce the answer unaided.

remediation.explanation: Recognition is matching an answer you see; recall is producing one from nothing. Practise producing.

label: Judges methods by how smooth they feel
description: The learner prefers blocked, fluent practice and avoids mixed or effortful practice because it feels worse.

remediation.explanation: Blocked, easy practice feels better and tests worse. Judge methods by delayed recall, not session comfort.

label: Reads all difficulty as failure
description: The learner concludes that struggle means the method or teacher is bad, when some difficulty is what builds retention.

remediation.explanation: Spacing, mixing, and retrieval all feel worse and work better. Effortless is not the goal; eventual success is.

label: Concludes ability is fixed from early struggle
description: The learner reads hard weeks as evidence of a fixed limit ('not a maths person') and stops investing effort.

remediation.explanation: Skill tracks accumulated practice. 'I am not an X person' ends learning early; 'my method needs work' continues it.

label: Believes more hours always mean more learning
description: The learner extends sessions, skips breaks and sleep, or stacks make-up marathons, ignoring diminishing returns and consolidation.

remediation.explanation: Hours matter less than what happens in them and after them: sleep, spacing, and retrieval beat raw time.

label: Counts stored notes as knowing
description: The learner treats writing, copying, or collecting material as having learned it.

remediation.explanation: Notes store information outside your head. The test is what you can produce without them.

label: Believes experience creates a permanent recording
description: The learner assumes watching or attending means the material is stored and accessible.

remediation.explanation: Experience writes a weak trace, not a recording. Traces fade without recall and strengthen with it.

label: Reads normal forgetting as personal failure
description: The learner treats each lapse as evidence the method or the person failed, rather than as the expected curve.

remediation.explanation: Forgetting is the default curve, not a defect. Each review bends it; each failed attempt still helps.

label: Equates verbatim memorisation with understanding
description: The learner memorises definitions word for word and cannot apply them in new contexts.

remediation.explanation: Verbatim recall without connections is brittle. Explain in your own words first, then memorise the details.

label: Waits to feel motivated before starting
description: The learner postpones sessions until motivation arrives, though action usually produces the feeling.

remediation.explanation: Action creates motivation more often than it receives it. Start with a two-minute version and let momentum argue for you.

label: Believes failed recall attempts are wasted effort
description: The learner avoids guessing or attempting answers they might get wrong, missing that the attempt itself aids learning.

remediation.explanation: A failed retrieval attempt primes the correct answer. Guessing with the source closed is not wasted; it is the workout.
